title: Surjective etale polynomial cover solving an Artin-Schreier equation
statement: Let U be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], p a prime with p = 0 in its ring of global functions, and t a global function. There exists a scheme V and an etale surjective morphism f:V→U, and a global function ω on V such that ω^p-ω=f^*t. No affineness or nonemptiness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Opening sequence of Tag 0A3J; polynomial-cover proof as in Tag 03PL with F=T^p-T-t and derivative -1.

proof.text: If the global section ring is zero, use the identity cover and the zero function. Otherwise F=T^p-T-t is monic of positive degree p and has derivative -1. The standard etale pair (F,1) has its algebra isomorphic to AdjoinRoot F, by explicit mutually inverse root maps. It is therefore etale. AdjoinRoot F is faithfully flat since F is monic of positive degree, hence its spectrum is surjective. This adapts the polynomial-cover proof of Stacks 03PL to the Artin-Schreier polynomial.

Base change Spec AdjoinRoot F → Spec Γ(U,O_U) along U.toSpecΓ. Both etaleness and surjectivity survive base change. Pull the root back along the second projection using ΓSpecIso. The polynomial equation and the commutativity of the square on global sections prove ω^p-ω=f^*t. This is implemented using Scheme.pullback_fst_toSpecΓ_appTop.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_etale_surjective_artinSchreier_eq_appTop {U : Scheme.{u}}
    (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hchar : (p : Γ(U, ⊤)) = 0) (t : Γ(U, ⊤)) :
    ∃ (V : Scheme.{u}) (f : V ⟶ U), Etale f ∧ Surjective f ∧
      ∃ ω : Γ(V, ⊤), ω ^ p - ω = f.appTop t
